body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a top story that has many in our community concerned: a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game. We’ll have more on that in a moment. Right now, the temperature at Meadows Field is 97°, and we’re looking at a high near 103° today. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64.

## The Kern Overnight

The night brought a series of incidents across Kern County. The most serious call came just after midnight when a shooting was reported at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. A witness told officers they saw someone shot, and the suspect was described as a white male in his 40s to 50s wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle—possibly a Ford Explorer. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast. 

Earlier in the night, around 2:16 a.m., crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street. Flames were visible inside the single-story structure with heavy smoke showing, but multiple engines and a truck company brought the fire under control by about 2:25. 

Before that, just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision near Gosford Road and Harris Road left one vehicle on fire. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded to the scene—one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back—and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries from that collision are unknown at this time. 

Multiple reports of a grass fire along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road drew a heavy response, including engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer, and a helicopter. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. 

Elsewhere, around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect, described as about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos and wearing black shorts, a gray shirt, and white shoes, fled on foot northbound. 

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports** that a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game left nearby residents shaken, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene. The scene at Independence High School was chaotic as people tried to understand what had happened after gunshots rang out nearby. Erin Foster, who lives a few houses down from where the suspect was arrested, said she was in shock when she learned what had happened. "I like our little neighborhood. That's kind of scary. I have, like, goosebumps. That's kind of scary. And he's 15. Oh, my," Foster said. Foster said she was on her way to her fiancé's workplace when she noticed an unusual scene outside her home. "We couldn't get out of the garage. There was, like, a little Hispanic family sitting over here on. I'm sorry, on the side of the garage, but there were a cop car in these undercover cars, and I was like, 'We can't get out.' So we had to ask him to move, but it was just odd 'cause then they were still here when I came back," Foster said. She said the family remained outside for an extended period of time. "Just odd that there was, like, a little Hispanic family, like a little baby, and like a mom it looked like, and some two, like, toddler little girls, and it was just like, 'Why are they sitting on the side of my garage?'" Foster said. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Eric Celedon said Friday night football games are safe and acknowledged why some community members may be hesitant to attend future games. "So we understand why someone would be fearful to come out, but we want to really reiterate that these events are safe," Celedon said.

**KGET 17 tells us** that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School. Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim's family and urged anyone with information to come forward. "Our community is heartbroken by this senseless act of violence," Goh said. "We must come together to support one another and ensure that those responsible are held accountable."

**Bakersfield Now shares** that the Southwest Market canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after the fatal shooting. Organizers said they made the decision out of respect for the victim and to allow the community time to heal. "We believe it is important to take a step back and focus on the well-being of our students and families during this difficult time," the organizers said in a statement.

## Something good

**Bakersfield Now reports** that a local family is organizing a flea market to help raise funds for a prosthetic leg. The event aims to collect $8,900 to support Villafana. This is a heartwarming example of our community coming together to support one of our own.

## Coming up this week

There are several events and meetings happening in Kern County this week. On Tuesday, August 26, there will be a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. 

At the Fox Theater, there are several shows scheduled. Tonight, August 22, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform. On Tuesday, August 26, there will be a Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 event. On Thursday, August 28, Rodney Carrington will take the stage. On Friday, August 29, there will be two shows: CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. 

Be sure to check local listings for more details on these events and meetings.
